chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about a Muslim man who has a pasture (land) containing a mountain (rocky area) that is sold. His Muslim brother comes to him, and he has sheep and is in need of a mountain. Is it permissible for him to sell the mountain to him as he sells it to others, or should he prevent him from the mountain if he asks for it without a price? And what is his status regarding it, and what can he take? He said: It is not permissible for him to sell his mountain to his brother, because the mountain is not his mountain. Rather, it is permissible for him to sell it to a non-Muslim.

key_terms.جَبَلٌ: Mountain or rocky area within the land
key_terms.لَيْسَ جَبَلَهُ: It is not his mountain (distinct property)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a Muslim to sell the rocky mountainous part of his land to another Muslim?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a specific legal distinction in Islamic property law regarding communal resources, ruling that a Muslim cannot sell the grazing rights of a mountainous pasture to another Muslim, likely to preserve shared utility, whereas selling to a non-Muslim is permissible. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on preventing the monopolization of essential communal assets among the faithful while allowing flexibility in transactions with others. The ruling underscores the principle that certain property rights are tied to the religious identity of the transactor in the context of shared resources.
